name: language-decision-registry
purpose: Defines how this workspace should choose efficient implementation languages and runtimes for agent-platform, workspace-monitor, desktop productization, local services, CLIs, and performance-critical components.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry before starting a new coding project, adding a desktop app layer, moving Python work into a compiled runtime, or choosing between Rust, Go, TypeScript, Python, and Electron-style JavaScript.
how_to_read: Read default_direction first to understand the current platform recommendation.
Read runtime_roles to see where each language fits in this workspace.
Read decision_gates before choosing Rust, Go, Electron, or Python for a new component.
Read non_goals so language enthusiasm does not override maintainability or measurement.
Treat community signals as adoption/risk hints, not proof of correctness.
update_triggers: A platform component moves from Python/TypeScript into Rust or Go.
The desktop app framework decision changes between Tauri, Wails, Electron, native, or browser-only delivery.
Performance, startup time, binary size, memory use, concurrency, or installer size becomes a measurable blocker.
A new official runtime release changes build, packaging, safety, or interop trade-offs.
A prototype benchmark contradicts the current default direction.

structure_rules.rule: Keep agent reasoning, research, evaluation, document processing, and governance automation Python-first unless measured bottlenecks or packaging needs justify a compiled boundary.
structure_rules.reason: The current platform already uses Python for agent workflows and benefits from ecosystem breadth and fast iteration.

structure_rules.rule: Prefer Rust when the component is a Tauri desktop shell, security-sensitive native command boundary, low-memory local binary, or performance-critical indexing/parsing module with a stable contract.
structure_rules.reason: Rust offers memory safety without a garbage collector and aligns with Tauri's native backend model, but has a higher learning and implementation cost.

structure_rules.rule: Prefer Go when the component is a long-running local service, concurrent file watcher, network daemon, operational CLI, or simple cross-platform binary where build speed and maintainability matter more than maximum low-level control.
structure_rules.reason: Go was designed around software engineering concerns such as builds, dependencies, readability, tooling, and service-scale concurrency.

structure_rules.rule: Use TypeScript/React/Next.js for monitor UI, dashboard, deck-like HTML, and Vercel-ready web surfaces.
structure_rules.reason: The existing workspace-monitor is already Next.js-based and has the best fit for browser-rendered repository visualization.

structure_rules.rule: Do not migrate a component to Rust or Go solely because the language is generally efficient; record the bottleneck, target metric, prototype result, and rollback path first.
structure_rules.reason: Language rewrites add operating cost and can reduce iteration speed if the problem was I/O, architecture, query shape, or dependency design rather than runtime speed.

default_direction.summary: Use a hybrid platform: Python for agent logic, TypeScript/Next.js for web UI and monitor surfaces, Rust/Tauri as the preferred desktop shell prototype, and Go as the preferred option for simple long-running local services or operational CLIs.
default_direction.desktop_recommendation: Tauri-first remains the default desktop shell direction because the product wants a small installable desktop wrapper around existing web UI with a clear native command boundary.
default_direction.service_recommendation: Go should be evaluated first for a separate local daemon, file watcher, or network service because it is operationally simple and fast to build.
default_direction.performance_recommendation: Rust should be evaluated first for stable hot loops, native filesystem/index/search modules, security-sensitive local commands, and components where memory safety plus low overhead is worth extra complexity.
default_direction.do_not_change: Do not move core agent/research/evaluation logic out of Python until a measured bottleneck, distribution constraint, or security boundary requires it.

avoid_for: small standalone end-user binaries where Python runtime packaging dominates
CPU-heavy tight loops after profiling proves Python is the bottleneck
security-sensitive native OS command surfaces without an explicit process boundary
verification: package boundary review before desktop embedding

avoid_for: trusted native filesystem operations without a hardened bridge
CPU-heavy local indexing outside Web Worker or native boundary
secret-bearing desktop operations in renderer code
verification: browser or static export smoke test
secret and snapshot review before public deployment

avoid_for: high-churn product behavior that changes every day
logic that heavily depends on Python AI/research libraries
teams or workflows without Rust validation capacity
deep browser UI integration where the current Next.js surface already works
desktop frameworks where Wails ecosystem gaps block release gates
verification: Wails comparison only if Go owns the desktop shell

best_for: JavaScript-heavy desktop app needing mature desktop ecosystem
fast iteration when bundle size is less important
avoid_for: small background utility where bundle size and memory are central
local filesystem access without strict sandbox and context isolation
installers where private workspace data could be accidentally bundled

decision_gates.question: Is the component UI, agent logic, local service, native command bridge, or performance hot path?
decision_gates.default_answer: UI stays TypeScript/Next.js, agent logic stays Python, desktop shell starts with Rust/Tauri, local daemon starts with Go, hot native module starts with Rust.

decision_gates.question: What measured bottleneck requires a compiled language?
decision_gates.default_answer: If no measured bottleneck exists, optimize architecture, caching, query shape, or workflow before rewriting runtime.

decision_gates.question: Is the output a developer tool, local CLI, end-user desktop app, hosted web app, or reusable library?
decision_gates.default_answer: End-user desktop app favors Tauri-first; hosted web app favors Next.js; local CLI/service favors Go unless native safety/performance pushes Rust.

decision_gates.question: How will it interact with Python agents, repository files, secrets, and user workspace paths?
decision_gates.default_answer: Keep process boundaries explicit. Do not embed secrets or scan arbitrary folders silently.

decision_gates.question: Which runtime will be easiest to maintain, test, debug, package, and hand to future agents?
decision_gates.default_answer: Choose the simplest runtime that passes release gates and performance targets.

non_goals: Do not rewrite Python agent workflows in Rust or Go for language preference alone.
Do not choose Electron by default if a small desktop shell is enough.
Do not choose Tauri by default when the required backend is mostly a Go service and Wails satisfies release gates better.
Do not treat GitHub stars, Reddit praise, or benchmark anecdotes as proof without local prototype measurements.
Do not introduce a compiled runtime without project-local install audit and rollback plan when dependencies are installed.
